text:
morgan: Heads up — customer-omega (private VPC) is seeing intermittent KMS decrypt failures and keystore-proxy 504s, pods restart looped once. Observed around 08:17 UTC. Posting a small excerpt of logs we captured from the keystore-proxy sidecar. :eyes:

morgan: ```
2024-08-21T08:17:03Z keystore-proxy ERROR decrypt request timeout id=abc123 backend=awskms status=504
2024-08-21T08:17:08Z keystore-proxy WARN retrying decrypt id=abc123 attempt=2
2024-08-21T08:17:18Z keystore-proxy ERROR decrypt failed id=abc123 error="dial tcp: i/o timeout"
```

morgan: This is on an on-prem-ish customer (VPC peers to our control plane). They recently tightened egress netpols. Could be related to that or IAM role scoping. 

priya: Thanks for the signal, Morgan. First q: is this limited to that customer/cluster?

morgan: so far only customer-omega. We reproduced by tightening egress in staging to match their netpol and saw similar timeouts.

sam: probable cause: keystore-proxy needs to reach the KMS endpoint and also our audit-ingest endpoint (datadog/splunk). If netpols block the egress or DNS to those endpoints, decrypts can hang until TCP timeout. We rolled a change last week that default-netpols deny egress by default.

priya: ok. Two parallel vectors: 1) network policy exceptions (allow egress to kms endpoints & logging), and 2) RBAC/service-account permissions — ensure keystore-proxy SA only has kms:Decrypt but also has sts:AssumeRole to the correct role if cross-account.

morgan: customers' infra teams are uncomfortable opening wide 0.0.0.0/0 egress. They want minimal IPs/hostnames we can document. Any recommended pattern?

sam: prefer FQDN-based egress via CNI egress proxy or DNS policies to allow hostnames like kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com or the private VPC endpoint IPs. For on-prem HSM, allow the HSM mgmt IPs. Example NetworkPolicy snippet that worked in staging (only allow egress to KMS and audit):

sam: ```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: keystore-egress-only
  namespace: redwood-keystore
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-proxy
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.100.0/24   # company VPC endpoint range
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          logging: allowed
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

priya: That looks good. Also add an annotation on the keystore-proxy deployment to emit verbose audit logs for decrypt failures so we can correlate request IDs. e.g., `keystore.redwood.io/audit=high`.

morgan: Should we also change RBAC to require an explicit RoleBinding for the keystore-proxy SA instead of relying on cluster-wide permissive bindings?

priya: Yes — tighten the SA scope. Make a new namespace-scoped role with just `get,list,watch` on secrets (if necessary) and a custom permission to call the keystore API. Keep the KMS permissions external (IAM).

sam: One more operational note: if the keystore-proxy cannot reach KMS it currently retries for up to 30s which pushes callers into higher latency SLO breaches. We should modify retry policy and surface a clear metric (keystore_proxy.decrypt.latency, keystore_proxy.decrypt.failures) to the console and set an alert.

morgan: Agreed. For customer-omega I added an emergency exception to their netpol to allow the VPC endpoint + splunk ingest; they saw immediate stability. We should make a hardened recommendation doc + a minimal Kubernetes policy bundle.

taylor: From incident triage POV: categorize this as sev-2 for customer-facing availability. Create a runbook step: if keystore-proxy 5xxs spike, check netpols -> check DNS resolution to KMS endpoint -> check IAM role assume logs -> escalate. Can someone open a JIRA with those steps + owners?

morgan: I'll open SEC-2148 and link the runbook. https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SEC-2148 (created). Assigning sam for netpol bundle, priya for RBAC and audit changes, taylor to update runbooks and alerts.

priya: For audit logging: ensure decrypt request/response events include principal, namespace, pod, request_id, and whether the request was proxied. Also ship to a tamper-evident store with 90d retention for private deployments. We'll need a config flag in the private-controlplane to toggle high-fidelity audit (default off, opt-in).

sam: Implementation notes: for VPC/private customers we can recommend either: 1) VPC endpoint for KMS + route table entries, or 2) a tightly-scoped NAT/IP allowlist + egress-proxy. Document both. For on-prem HSM integrate with our keystore adapter that speaks PKCS11 — ensure netpol to HSM mgmt port 15000 is open.

sec-bot: [Automated] Alert linked: SEC-2148 created by morgan. Current status: investigating. Related alerts: keystore_proxy.decrypt.failures (spike), netpol.denied_egress (seen).

morgan: Action items summary: 
- sam: publish `keystore-netpol-bundle.yaml` w/ FQDN/IP examples and test matrix (due EOD Tue)
- priya: prepare RBAC Role/RoleBinding templates + audit flag proposal (due Wed)
- taylor: update runbook + add alerts to console (due Wed)
- morgan: coordinate with customer-omega, verify patch in staging (done)

priya: One more security check — let's avoid leaking KMS ARNs in pod logs. Mask request metadata fields except request_id and anonymized principal.

sam: I'll also add a quick `kubectl` check command we can run during incidents: `kubectl exec -n redwood-keystore -it deploy/keystore-proxy -- curl -vs https://kms.internal.example.com/health`

morgan: ok thanks all. we'll do a short sync tomorrow 14:00 UTC to walk through the netpol bundle before we publish. :thumbsup:
